_comment: The canonical sound asset registry. An asset is identified by its NAME and nothing
else: sfx_chair_roll_fast is the same asset in Chapter 1, in Chapter 27 and in the
Godot game. Assets never belong to playback positions; audio/cues/chapter-NN.json
says where they play. Same philosophy as the voice clip cache.
NOTHING HERE HAS BEEN GENERATED. Every asset is a PROPOSAL awaiting Joshua's
approval; `approved: false` and no audio file exists. Generation is manual and
intentional (scripts/audio.py generate-sfx) and is never wired to a push.
`source`: "generated" means ElevenLabs makes it from `prompt`. "supplied" means a
human put the file there; it has no prompt, it is fingerprinted by its own bytes,
and generation never runs for it.
`assetVersion` is the deliberate-retake lever. Bumping it invalidates that ONE
asset, which is how an approved sound gets replaced without touching any other.
Prompt discipline, from Joshua's brief: ambience carries no voices, no music, no
prominent alarms, no footsteps and no cinematic gestures. Those are event sounds and
live as their own assets so they can be moved, retuned or switched off separately.
MEASURED LEVELS, 2026-09-18. scripts/measure-mix.py decoded every asset because
Joshua could not hear the typing even with all nine cues resolving. The finding is
not about the mixer: nine of the twenty assets came back 40 to 63 dB below full
scale in RMS, which no gain can rescue against speech at about -22 dB.
The pattern is my prompts' fault, and it is consistent. Every prompt carrying a
LOUDNESS word -- soft, quiet, subtle, faint, barely perceptible -- came back nearly
silent; every prompt carrying an ENERGY word -- erupting, sharp, urgent, firm --
came back hot. The provider read those adjectives as absolute level rather than as
character. A prompt should describe the sound's character and its microphone
distance, and leave the level to the mix, where a number costs nothing to change.
`soundsForSeconds` is the time the RMS envelope stays within 20 dB of the asset's
own peak. 0.00 on a 3-second file means a couple of transients in near-silence --
which is what the keyboard is, and why more gain would only make faint ticks
louder rather than making typing audible.
THE CORRECTED PROMPT STYLE, TESTED 2026-09-18. The eight assets chapters 2 and 3
added were written the new way -- character plus microphone distance, an explicit
"recorded at a strong present level", and not one loudness adjective -- and then
measured the same way. Five came back usable (-16.7 to -28.5 dBFS RMS), two came
back quiet, and one came back at -64.7, the lowest reading in the whole set. So the
style helps -- nine of twenty failed before, one of eight now -- but it is not the
whole rule, and the three that missed say what the rest of it is.
A SUBJECT THAT IS FAR AWAY, OR THAT IS DEFINED BY ITS OWN ABSENCE, IS RENDERED THAT
WAY, AND "recorded at a strong present level" DOES NOT OVERRIDE IT. The three:
sfx_boundary_event_collapse  -64.7   "pulled away into total silence",
"ending in absolute nothing"
sfx_distant_vibration_deep   -38.9   "from somewhere far outside", "felt through
the structure rather than heard"
amb_settlement_sirens        -34.3   "heard from indoors through walls and
glass", "at different distances"
The five that landed all describe something close, present and physical: rings
turning on bearings, a chirp on a wrist, a floor shuddering, a lever thrown, sound
slamming back into a room.
So the rule is: DESCRIBE THE SOUND AS IT REACHES THE MICROPHONE, not where it came
from. A siren through a wall is a muffled siren AT the microphone -- low-passed,
close, filling the frame -- not a siren somewhere else. A collapse into silence is
the last half second of sound and the pressure change, at the microphone; silence
itself cannot be generated loud, and asking for it gets a file of it.
THE RETAKE, 2026-09-18, on Joshua's approval. The ten assets measured too quiet to
rescue with gain had their prompts rewritten against both lessons above and their
`assetVersion` bumped to 2, which invalidates those ten and nothing else. Their old
readings are kept as `previousMeasured` so the before and after sit side by side.
Every one of the ten carried a loudness word -- "quiet", "soft", "faint", "barely
perceptible", "very low level", "gentle", "understated". Where the old prompt used
one to mean CHARACTER, the new prompt says the character directly: "low urgency"
became "sounding once and not repeating", "soft steady ventilation" became "moving
ventilation air", "light, quiet contact" became "rubbery contact with a broad low
thud under it". Pace and timbre survive; the level does not get asked for.
The keyboard is the one whose CONTENT, not only its level, was wrong: 0.00 seconds
within 20 dB of its own peak, a couple of ticks in near-silence. Its new prompt asks
for keystrokes "without a gap for the whole recording, about six a second", with no
fade in and no fade out, because the old one said "a short burst" and got one.
GAINS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT RETUNED IN THE SAME PASS. The current numbers were set
against near-silent files; the right ones follow from measuring the retakes, which
is free. Generate, measure, then tune -- not guess twice.
THE RETAKE'S RESULT, MEASURED. Five of the ten came good and five did not, and the
split is not about wording. It is about WHAT KIND OF SOUND was asked for.
DISCRETE EVENTS, all rescued by the rewrite:
sfx_boundary_event_collapse  -64.7 -> -20.4   (+44.3 dB)
sfx_equipment_power_up_soft  -63.1 -> -28.0   (+35.1 dB)
sfx_system_notify_soft       -42.6 -> -24.0   (+18.6 dB)
sfx_footsteps_sarah_sneakers -54.3 -> -38.2   (+16.1 dB)
sfx_console_tone_soft        -54.5 -> -40.1   (+14.4 dB)
CONTINUOUS OR REPEATING TEXTURES, none rescued:
amb_tombs_lab_night          -47.8 -> -42.5   (+5.3)
amb_intercom_channel_open    -52.2 -> -47.5   (+4.7)
sfx_keyboard_typing_short    -46.9 -> -42.6   (+4.3)
sfx_chair_roll_slow          -47.4 -> -46.7   (+0.7)
sfx_chair_roll_fast          -44.4 -> -48.3   (-3.9, WORSE)
A one-off event gets rendered at whatever level the prompt's language implies, so
fixing the language fixes the level. A continuous bed, a hiss, a castor rumble or a
stream of keystrokes comes back near the noise floor whatever the prompt says. Two
rounds of prompt work moved the second group by an average of 2 dB. THAT IS THE
LIMIT OF PROMPTING, not a wording that has not been found yet, and a third round of
rewrites would be the "random replacements" Joshua's brief says not to buy.
TWO ASSETS ALSO CAME BACK WORSE IN SHAPE, not only in level:
- sfx_chair_roll_fast lost its peak as well (-21.5 -> -26.8).
- amb_tombs_lab_night's envelope is no longer even: `soundsForSeconds` fell from
20.00 to 5.50, so it now has a loud middle and quiet ends. That is a worse LOOP
than the one it replaced, whatever its RMS says.
The keyboard is still the one whose CONTENT is wrong: 0.00 seconds within 20 dB of
its own peak after a prompt that explicitly asked for keystrokes with no gap for the
whole recording, about six a second. The peak rose 8.6 dB, so the individual clicks
are louder; they are still isolated clicks.
Footwear comes from the chapter's visual canon, so footsteps can eventually be
chosen from character/outfit metadata rather than picked by hand at each cue.
Kept to one field per character on purpose: there is no outfit system yet and
building one before a chapter needs it would be inventing a problem.
Jack has a profile but NO asset. He is seated for the whole of Chapter 1 and never
walks, so generating his footsteps now would be paying for silence.

jack-bennett.notes: Seated throughout Chapter 1. Assign an asset when a chapter actually walks him.

sarah-bennett.notes: Gray sneakers, not heels. She enters the laboratory and crosses to Jack.

amb_tombs_lab_night.prompt: Room tone of a clean research laboratory at night, microphone standing in the room. Moving ventilation air, a continuous electrical hum from racked equipment, cooling fans turning, and a fine high shimmer from instruments on standby. Enclosed and filling the frame, recorded at a strong present level. Even throughout so it loops. No voices, no music, no alarms, no beeping, no footsteps.
amb_tombs_lab_night.notes: The one environmental bed for Chapter 1. The whole chapter is Jack's laboratory; there is no location change in the manuscript, so there is no second bed. Its prompt is deliberately terse: the first version was 476 characters and was rejected twice with HTTP 400, at 22 seconds and again at 20, while every other asset -- including a 20-second looping bed -- generated fine at 385 characters or fewer. The cause was prompt LENGTH, not duration. Nothing substantive was dropped, only words.
amb_tombs_lab_night.promptStyle: retake-2026-09-18: character and mic distance only, no loudness adjective, described at the microphone

amb_console_alarm_bed.prompt: A repeating electronic security alarm inside a laboratory, heard as a continuous background state rather than a single event. Insistent two-note warning tone cycling steadily with an even gap between repeats, slightly hard-edged and synthetic, with a faint room reflection. Consistent volume, no build, no crescendo, no siren sweep, no voices, no music. Even throughout so it can loop.
amb_console_alarm_bed.notes: Categorised `alarm`, not `ambience`, so switching ambience off does not silence the chapter's alarm. Loops under the opening sequence and is ducked hard beneath speech.

amb_intercom_channel_open.prompt: An intercom speaker with the line open and nobody talking, microphone right at the grille. Narrow-band electrical hiss with a steady carrier hum under it, band-limited and boxy the way a small wall-mounted speaker colours everything. Filling the frame, recorded at a strong present level. Even throughout so it loops. No voices, no speech, no music, no clicks, no tones.
amb_intercom_channel_open.notes: The cheapest honest way to tell the listener Sarah is on a speaker and not in the room. It sits under her intercom lines without touching her approved voice clips, which are never filtered or regenerated for this.
amb_intercom_channel_open.promptStyle: retake-2026-09-18: character and mic distance only, no loudness adjective, described at the microphone

amb_tombs_array_power_rise.prompt: A very large machine beginning to draw power somewhere below and far away. Deep sub-bass hum rising slowly in pitch and intensity, layered with a distant electrical charging whine and a faint sense of enormous mass energising. Restrained and ominous, felt more than heard, no impact, no explosion, no siren, no voices, no music, no cinematic riser or trailer hit.
amb_tombs_array_power_rise.notes: The tension spine of the last third, and the beginning of the TOMBS Array's own sound identity. It enters when the remote initialization request appears and does not leave.

sfx_console_tone_soft.prompt: A two-tone electronic blip from a laboratory console, microphone close to the speaker. Two rounded mid-range notes with a clean decay, synthetic and warm rather than piercing, sounding once and not repeating. Filling the frame, recorded at a strong present level, with a little room reflection. No alarm, no siren, no voices, no music.
sfx_console_tone_soft.notes: The polite tone that fails to wake Jack. Used twice in Chapter 1 -- the second, louder tone is this same asset at a higher gain, which is what the manuscript describes.
sfx_console_tone_soft.promptStyle: retake-2026-09-18: character and mic distance only, no loudness adjective, described at the microphone

sfx_console_alarm_erupt.prompt: A laboratory console suddenly erupting into full alarm. Several electronic alert tones firing at once and overlapping into an urgent layered warning, sharp onset, hard and synthetic, with a short tail of room reflection. No siren sweep, no voices, no music, no explosion.
sfx_console_alarm_erupt.notes: The single biggest sound event in the chapter. The escalation from one chirp to this is the whole opening beat.

sfx_alert_warning_hit.prompt: One sharp electronic warning tone announcing a new alert on a laboratory display. Single hard synthetic alert stab, urgent and attention-grabbing, short decay, slight room reflection. One hit only, no repeats, no siren, no voices, no music.
sfx_alert_warning_hit.notes: A single interruption, distinct from the polite chirp and from the full eruption. Used twice: the second alarm during the trace, and the tone that interrupts the couple much later.

sfx_system_notify_soft.prompt: A single electronic notification from a computer acting on its own, microphone close to the speaker. One rounded mid-range blip with a short clean tail, followed by a brief digital interface flourish, sounding once and not repeating. Filling the frame, recorded at a strong present level, with a little room around it. Not an alarm, no voices, no music.
sfx_system_notify_soft.notes: Deliberately calm. The unsettling thing about TOMBS opening its own directory is how unbothered it sounds. Used twice: the directory opening itself, and the file opening itself.
sfx_system_notify_soft.promptStyle: retake-2026-09-18: character and mic distance only, no loudness adjective, described at the microphone

sfx_terminal_lock_engage.prompt: A computer terminal locking. A firm confirming electronic click-clunk with a short descending two-tone confirmation, then the display going dark with a faint electrical fade. Decisive and final, close-mic. No alarm, no voices, no music.
sfx_terminal_lock_engage.notes: Jack taking control back. It has to sound like it worked, so that the terminal coming back on by itself lands as a violation.

sfx_equipment_power_up_soft.prompt: A display and the equipment behind it coming back on, microphone at the machine. An energising swell with a rising high-frequency whine settling into a steady hum, and a capacitive tick as the panel wakes. One unhurried movement, close-mic, filling the frame, recorded at a strong present level. No alarm, no beeping, no voices, no music.
sfx_equipment_power_up_soft.notes: The terminal undoing Jack's lock without being asked. Soft on purpose: a bang would make it an attack, and the point is that it is calm.

sfx_intercom_open.prompt: An intercom being keyed on. A firm mechanical button press followed immediately by a small electrical pop and the channel opening into a thin live speaker hiss. Close-mic, tactile. No voices, no speech, no music, no tones.
sfx_intercom_open.notes: Marks the acoustic frame Sarah's remote voice arrives in. Used twice: reaching for the intercom, and tapping the button again.

sfx_intercom_static.prompt: A burst of static from an intercom speaker with no answer. Uneven narrow-band crackle and hiss through a small speaker grille, rising briefly and falling away to nothing. Thin and boxy. No voices, no speech, no music, no tones.
sfx_intercom_static.notes: The manuscript makes static the ANSWER to Jack's question, so this is dialogue's turn in the scene, not decoration.

sfx_intercom_close.prompt: An intercom channel closing. A light mechanical release click and the live speaker hiss cutting away to room silence. Close-mic, small and final. No voices, no speech, no music, no tones.
sfx_intercom_close.notes: Closes the frame the intercom opened. Without it the listener has no cue that the channel is gone, and the room's silence afterward is part of the scene.

sfx_lab_door_slide.prompt: An automatic laboratory door sliding open. A soft pneumatic release, a smooth mechanical glide along a track, and a light settling clunk as it reaches the end of its travel. Clean modern facility, close but with room reflection behind it. No voices, no music, no alarm.
sfx_lab_door_slide.notes: Someone entering behind Jack while he is looking the other way. Pure spatial information, and the manuscript puts it mid-sentence on purpose.

sfx_footsteps_sarah_sneakers.prompt: Four or five footsteps of an adult in rubber-soled sneakers on a hard smooth laboratory floor, microphone at floor level beside them. Rubbery contact with a broad low thud under it and no heel click, an even walking gait. Close and filling the frame, recorded at a strong present level, with modest room reflection. No voices, no music, no heels, no hard shoes, no boots.
sfx_footsteps_sarah_sneakers.notes: Sarah's gray sneakers, per Chapter 1 visual canon -- explicitly not heels. Used twice and only for spatial transitions: entering the laboratory, and crossing the room to Jack. The listener never hears her walk otherwise.
sfx_footsteps_sarah_sneakers.promptStyle: retake-2026-09-18: character and mic distance only, no loudness adjective, described at the microphone

sfx_chair_roll_fast.prompt: An office chair on castors shoved hard backward across a hard floor, microphone right at the castors. A fast scuff, castors rumbling over a smooth surface with the frame rattling above them, and an abrupt stop. Physical and close, filling the frame, recorded at a strong present level, with room reflection. No voices, no music, no crash, no breaking.
sfx_chair_roll_fast.notes: Jack waking so hard the chair moves. It gives the alarm a physical consequence in a body rather than only on a screen.

sfx_chair_roll_slow.notes: Two people arranging themselves around one workstation. Used twice: Sarah pulling a second chair over, and Jack rolling sideways to make room. Consciously different from the fast roll -- that one is a startle, this one is a marriage.

sfx_keyboard_typing_short.prompt: Continuous fast typing on a low-profile computer keyboard, microphone directly over the keys. Keystrokes landing without a gap for the whole recording, about six a second, each a crisp plastic click with the dense clatter of the key bed under it. No pauses, no fade in, no fade out. Filling the frame, recorded at a strong present level. No voices, no music, no beeping, no mouse clicks.
sfx_keyboard_typing_short.notes: Used three times, only where the manuscript actually starts or resumes typing. It marks who has the keyboard, which is how the scene's authority shifts from Jack to Sarah.

sfx_access_denied_tone.prompt: A system refusing a command. One short blunt descending two-note electronic rejection tone, flat and unsympathetic, close-mic with slight room. Final but not an alarm. No voices, no music, no siren.
sfx_access_denied_tone.notes: Used twice, before each Request denied. Hearing the same refusal twice is the information: Jack tried again and got nowhere.

sfx_access_revoked_tone.prompt: A system locking a user out for good. A heavier descending electronic tone with a low weighted thud underneath it and a short cold decay, more serious and more final than an ordinary rejection. Close-mic with slight room. No voices, no music, no siren, no alarm.
sfx_access_revoked_tone.notes: Distinct from the denial tone on purpose. The story distinguishes being refused from being locked out, and that difference is the chapter's ending; it should not sound the same.

sfx_wrist_terminal_chirp.prompt: An incoming call alert on a small wrist-worn device. Two rising electronic notes with a short clean decay, close to the microphone, recorded at a strong present level with plenty of body. Distinct from a desk console: smaller, tighter, worn on a person. No voices, no music, no alarm.
sfx_wrist_terminal_chirp.notes: Jack's wrist terminal, which carries every call with Lena across chapters 2 and 3. It needs to read as a different device from the laboratory console.
sfx_wrist_terminal_chirp.promptStyle: corrected-2026-09-18: character and mic distance only, explicit strong present level, no loudness adjectives

sfx_array_rings_move.prompt: Large articulated machinery rotating. Heavy rings turning on precision bearings with a deep servo drive under them, metal sliding against metal, a sense of considerable mass moving under control. Full-bodied and close, recorded at a strong present level. No voices, no music, no alarm, no impact.
sfx_array_rings_move.notes: The TOMBS Array's rings, the signature machine sound of chapter 2. Loops because the manuscript has them moving, stopping and starting again across the whole scene.
sfx_array_rings_move.promptStyle: corrected-2026-09-18: character and mic distance only, explicit strong present level, no loudness adjectives

sfx_shutdown_lever_pull.prompt: A heavy industrial disconnect lever thrown by hand, followed by electrical power dropping out of a room. A solid mechanical clack with weight behind it, then the collapse of every hum and fan into silence. Close and physical, recorded at a strong present level. No voices, no music.
sfx_shutdown_lever_pull.notes: Jack's physical shutdown. It has to sound conclusive, because the room coming back on afterwards is the moment TOMBS stops being a malfunction.
sfx_shutdown_lever_pull.promptStyle: corrected-2026-09-18: character and mic distance only, explicit strong present level, no loudness adjectives

amb_settlement_sirens.prompt: Civil emergency sirens across a small town, heard from indoors through walls and glass. Several units at different distances, rising and falling out of step with each other, with the building muffling the high end. Even and continuous, recorded at a strong present level. No voices, no music, no interior alarm.
amb_settlement_sirens.notes: Once Jack orders the settlement-wide emergency the sirens do not stop. Heard from inside, which is where both chapters stay.
amb_settlement_sirens.promptStyle: corrected-2026-09-18: character and mic distance only, explicit strong present level, no loudness adjectives

sfx_boundary_event_collapse.prompt: An electrical charge rising over a room, then the whole air of that room compressing inward in one second, the way a hatch sealing on a pressurised chamber pulls at your ears. A deep inward suck with the room's hum bending downward in pitch as it goes. Close and enveloping, filling the frame, recorded at a strong present level. No voices, no music, no impact, no explosion.
sfx_boundary_event_collapse.notes: The event itself. The manuscript is explicit that the sound does not fade or muffle, it ceases, so the asset has to end in real silence rather than a tail.

sfx_boundary_event_return.notes: The other half of the event. These two are always used as a pair, with the silence between them carried by the manifest's own pause rather than by either file.
sfx_boundary_event_return.promptStyle: corrected-2026-09-18: character and mic distance only, explicit strong present level, no loudness adjectives

sfx_building_shake.prompt: A building structure shuddering. Low-frequency rumble through a concrete floor with light fittings and loose equipment rattling above it, building and then easing. Interior perspective, recorded at a strong present level with real low end. No voices, no music, no collapse, no debris.
sfx_building_shake.notes: The shake that makes Sarah catch herself against the console. Used where the manuscript shakes the building, not as general tension.
sfx_building_shake.promptStyle: corrected-2026-09-18: character and mic distance only, explicit strong present level, no loudness adjectives

sfx_distant_vibration_deep.prompt: A deep vibration arriving from somewhere far outside a building and passing through it. Sub-bass swell with a slow approach and a slower departure, felt through the structure rather than heard as an event, like distant thunder with no crack. Recorded at a strong present level with real low end. No voices, no music, no impact.
sfx_distant_vibration_deep.notes: The unexplained vibration that arrives twice at the end of chapter 3 and that Jack decides he does not want to explain. The single most important new asset: it is the first sound of the giant world and it will recur for a long time.
sfx_distant_vibration_deep.promptStyle: corrected-2026-09-18: character and mic distance only, explicit strong present level, no loudness adjectives
